newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on strong sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on strong sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended sharply up on Thursday on strong sentiment boosted by the breaching of the key 80-point resistance level with domestic investors seen as the biggest buyers, brokers said.
The B index surged 5.522 points or 7.18 percent to 82.392 points on huge volume of 57.12 million shares worth $29.10 million, compared with $15.07 million on Wednesday.
Large scale buying by local speculators pushed prices up suddenly in the afternoon session, although foreign capital was also seen moving into the market, brokers said.
"With domestic A shares seen as being high-priced, some domestic players shifted their interest to the B share market, which caused today's surge in the B index," one broker said.
The B index, which up sharply in recent months, has still been overshadowed by the A index, which is up over 40 percent on the start of the year.
"Domestic investors rushed in to buy without giving any thought to the results of the firms," another broker said. "They are only aiming at quick profits."
Upward potential will be limited on Friday with technical charts showing signs of a need for a correction, brokers said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 41 up, one flat and one down.
Huangshan Tourism Development was the star on institutional buying, surging $0.066 or 10.00 percent to $0.726 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkai Chemical was the most actively traded, gaining $0.014 or 4.51 percent to $0.324 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index closed down on a technical correction after sharp gains over the past few months, but market sentiment was still good, brokers said.
The index dipped 7.141 points or 0.51 percent to 1,384.788 points on volume of 695.2 million shares worth 8.5 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index fell 21.481 points or 0.60 percent to 3,571.814 points.
Cangzhou Chemical Industry was the biggest loser after it posted poor 1996 results, slipping 1.50 yuan or 9.18 percent to 14.83 yuan on volume of 3.2 million shares.
